# Installation {#sec-installation}

## Review workstation

The supported Windows lifecycle is `SETUP.cmd` -> `START.cmd` -> browser. No
machine-wide Administrator access is required. `uv` owns the project-managed
Python 3.12 environment; Node.js is taken from a compatible system install or
from the official no-admin fallback under ignored `local-state/tools/`.

```{=latex}
\Needspace{18\baselineskip}
```

**Steps (Windows).**

```text
git clone https://github.com/siriponsri/dr-support-screening-poc.git
cd dr-support-screening-poc
SETUP.cmd
START.cmd
```

**Expected result.** The workstation serves `http://127.0.0.1:8000/app/` and
opens it in the default browser. Daily `START.cmd` calls reuse the project
environment and frontend dependencies. It rebuilds the frontend only when the
tracked source signature or lockfile state requires it; it never runs `npm ci`
on a normal start. Use `OPEN_APP.cmd` to reopen the app and `STOP.cmd` to stop
only the repository-managed process.

Use `SETUP.cmd --check` for a read-only installation diagnostic and
`SETUP.cmd --dev` when test, DICOM, and browser-test extras are required.

## Linux server checkout

Place the release at `/opt/dr-support-screening-poc` when using the included systemd unit. Keep runtime assets in `local-state/` or another private path. Never commit model weights, review databases, or secret environment files.

## Configuration

Use `.env.example` only as a reference. Supply tokens through the private process environment or an approved secret manager. The model-server example is `deployment/model-server.env.example`; `docs/operations/CONFIGURATION.md` lists every variable and its safe default.
